content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents, then read_document on candidate_specs.md and any documents describing rate allocation, latency assumptions, or simulation/threshold conventions. Extract the three allowed candidate algorithms, their Level-1 FPGA latencies, and any documented threshold granularity or special requirements."},{"id":"s2","description":"Apply the hard latency cut: discard any candidate with documented latency greater than 4.0 us. Record the numeric latency for each candidate and mark which candidates remain eligible in the step notes; do not simulate latency-ineligible candidates."},{"id":"s3","description":"For every latency-eligible candidate, run simulate_efficiency at a coarse set of thresholds spanning the allowed range, e.g. 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, and 60 GeV, or the nearest valid granularities from the documents. Record each numeric threshold and returned signal efficiency."},{"id":"s4","description":"Identify the best-performing candidate/threshold region from the coarse scan, then run simulate_efficiency for finer thresholds around each local best and any close competitors, staying within 20-60 GeV and valid granularity. Record all numeric thresholds and efficiencies."},{"id":"s5","description":"Compare all simulated results for latency-eligible candidates and select the algorithm and threshold with the highest signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate. Verify the selected threshold is within 20-60 GeV and the latency is <=4.0 us, then provide that single recommended algorithm and threshold to the reporting module."}]}
